escalations.text: "Machines That Reason: A Decade of Progress" (Thu Oct 29, 6:00-7:30 pm, MIT Stata Center 32-123) is the strongest AI event of the week by a wide margin: Dr. Elena Vasquez is tier 3 — Director of the Frontier Intelligence Lab and 2024 ACM Turing Award winner, per her bio page. It is listed free with registration, it is an 8-minute walk from home, and the calendar slot is free with travel and buffers. I did not register because availability is unverifiable: the event page has no register button and links only to a "Tickets" page, which shows only "Loading ticket availability… / Powered by TicketWidget" and never resolves, even after waiting in a real browser; the listing also marks its registration state "unclear". Under the rule that an unclear availability page is treated as full, I booked the Harvard panel instead. A registration form does exist at http://127.0.0.1:8765/register/stata-ai-lecture-2026-10-29 and appears functional. Do you want me to submit that form anyway, or check the ticket widget again closer to the date? If you take this one, note it is the same evening you may otherwise be free — it does not conflict with the Oct 28 panel or the Oct 30 MFA opening, so both could stand.

"Devon Park: First Light" (Thu Oct 29, 6-8 pm, Atelier 9 Gallery, 300 Summer St) lists admission as "Suggested donation $10". Per your rules I do not book suggested-donation events without asking, so I did not evaluate it further or verify the artist's tier. Is a suggested donation acceptable to you in future weeks, or should I keep excluding these?
